rules.title: No filler or coaching in a sentence
rules.text: Filler and reader-coaching — 'it is worth noting', 'in order to', 'basically', 'be sure to' — spend words on nothing the document has to say. The fact is the sentence; the phrase around it is the slop.

inspection.pattern: (?i)\b(it'?s worth (noting|mentioning)|needless to say|note that|keep in mind|as you can see|in order to|basically|essentially|at the end of the day|it is important to|be sure to|as (mentioned|noted) (above|earlier))\b

judgement.question: Is this filler or coaching — a phrase that could be deleted without losing a fact, a rule or a step — rather than a sentence the document needs?

criteria.true: the phrase adds no information: deleting it leaves the sentence's content unchanged
criteria.false: the phrase carries information (a condition, a reason, a source, a sequence), or it is inside a quotation
